active_experiment: Build a provenance-bound submission-time cohort manifest for at least two ICLR 2017-2022 years; review-aware empirical policy tests remain gated. Synthetic Stage A exists only as a non-evidentiary engineering fixture.
evidence_collected: Selective-label problem is established prior art and directly threatens naive retrospective policy evaluation.
Active learning already studies label allocation under expensive human-oracle budgets.
Published peer-review evidence does not support a blanket assumption that novelty is systematically suppressed.
Common novelty indicators are construct-sensitive and can overlap with interdisciplinarity.
Live acquisition probe returned HTTP 429 and then HTTP 403 from api.openreview.net; no corpus record was treated as acquired.
OpenReview documents supported API2 and legacy API1 retrieval for submissions, reviews, rebuttals and decisions.
Independent corpora demonstrate useful ICLR 2017-2022 coverage of submission metadata, decisions and reviews.
OpenReview-derived raw-note datasets expose note creation timestamps, but timestamps on surviving notes do not prove preservation of earlier edited states.
Historical crawler prior art explicitly models revisions of submissions and notes, providing a reconstruction lead that still requires provenance validation.
A field-by-year temporal observability matrix now separates coverage from decision-time admissibility and permits a narrower submission-time Track A without weakening review-aware Track B.
A deterministic synthetic allocation harness now tests equal-budget, no-leakage, uniqueness and reproducibility invariants without licensing empirical policy claims.
unresolved_methodological_risks: OpenReview interface/service availability and possible endpoint permissions; do not bypass source controls
decision-time review/version state may be irrecoverable for material portions of ICLR 2017-2022
submission title/abstract/keyword versions still require provenance binding before allocator use
selective labels and post-decision visibility effects
construct validity of epistemic value and novelty
future-information leakage through pretrained representations or metadata
synthetic benchmark conclusions are assumption-bound and must never be promoted as empirical evidence
adversarial_objections: The programme's headline mechanism substantially overlaps active learning, constrained ranking and exploration/exploitation.
Citation-based outcomes are treatment-affected proxies, not counterfactual intrinsic value.
Novelty suppression is an empirical question and existing journal evidence sometimes points in the opposite direction.
A current public record is not evidence that its decision-time value is reconstructable; a temporal firewall cannot recover overwritten history.
Creation timestamps are insufficient if note contents were subsequently edited and earlier revisions are absent.
Synthetic policy results can be manufactured by scenario assumptions; Stage A is therefore an engineering test, not evidence.
